research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
substitution rotation intervals and lineup spells
methodological_questions: How is offensive reorganization measured, and how is the baseline L defined without using post-absence data?
Is the association between reorganization and change in PPP detectable with 148 spells at the stated minimum detectable effect (rho)?
Do regression-to-the-mean, selection on absence timing, and lineup or opponent confounding bias the estimate?
Is player-level data complete in the graph database for every absence spell?

historical_evidence.finding: Pre-registered test on 23 player-season absences from 18 franchises. V1 (real absence moves the association structure) was confirmed (PAP-023: V1(b) +0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187]). V2 (simulation predicts the magnitude) was not confirmed (rho +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667]), with franchises below the registered floor of about 20. Record notes a later full-pool run reversed V2. Limited by small_sample.

Compared V4 and V5 player routing on observed PPP. 8 divergences, 0 scoreable; 8 unscored because players were missing from Neo4j, and V5 mostly routed to 'team'. Record notes data coverage could be checked before running. Failure type A_unanswerable.

Scanned 6,221 (offense, opponent, play type) cells for head-to-head leaders. The apparent edge (+1.26 PPP at n>=5, +1.13 at n>=15) came from low-n cells, e.g. 1-shot role players at 3.00 PPP. Records recommend keeping the n>=15 gate.

Live trigger timing in playoff replays (101 to 228 triggers). Early-vs-late BEST-AVOID gap (0.701 vs 0.415) rests on 26 early triggers. One record calls its p=0.031 (n=57) weak evidence. BEST vs AVOID p=0.073965 in the 10-series replay, confirmed in the 25-series replay.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Magnitude test (V2): whether a simulation predicts the size of the absence effect, on the 23-absence pool
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as not confirmed; CI spans zero and franchises fell below the registered floor of about 20, so the test was underpowered. A later full-pool run reversed V2.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-level PPP comparison across routing rules using graph-database player records
failed_approaches.why: Players were missing from Neo4j, so 0 of 8 divergences were scoreable; V5 mostly routed to 'team' rather than a player. Recorded as A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Head-to-head leader routing signal estimated from low-possession cells
failed_approaches.why: Apparent PPP edge was small-sample inflation (for example n=6, PPP=3.00). Recorded as artifact.
Gap rests on 26 early triggers; the record calls its evidence weak and the overall status inconclusive.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on absence and routing shows that small-n subsets (under about 30 units) repeatedly produced unstable or inflated effects, so a 148-spell design needs explicit power and subset rules.
Graph-database player coverage has failed before, so the data pipeline must be validated before any test.
Real absences moved an association structure in one pre-registered test (SF20 V1), which suggests the absence setting is worth studying, though it does not test this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record measures offensive reorganization relative to L or tests its link to change in PPP.
No retrieved record defines L, the reorganization index, or the stated minimum detectable effect value (rho).
No retrieved record reports a test of this question at the 148-spell or 986-unit scale.
The retrieved records are cut in places (SF20, SF31, SF04 full text not read), so details beyond the summaries are unverified.
own_inferences: With 148 spells, a two-sided alpha of 0.05 and 80% power, the detectable correlation is roughly |rho| of 0.23. A smaller effect cannot be resolved, so the stated MDE needs checking against this.
The unit count is ambiguous (986 vs 148 spells). A design that pools team-games inside spells would overstate the effective sample size unless clustering is handled.
Defining L from pre-absence games only and scoring reorganization in the post-absence window is the main protection against lookahead and regression-to-the-mean.
The question as posed is underspecified (L and reorganization undefined), so a competent test needs a pre-registered operational definition before any outcome is seen.
uncertainties: The definition of L, the reorganization metric, and its reliability across seasons are unknown.
The numeric MDE value is missing from the data description.
Whether all 148 spells have complete player-level graph records is unknown; SF-APPS-009 suggests gaps are possible.
Possession counts per spell are unknown, so exposure sparsity cannot be judged.
Playoff data for 2025-26 is complete as of 2026-11-01, but partial-season regular-season data should be excluded if used.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval turned up no direct prior test of this question, but it did show three repeated failure modes in this project (small-n artifacts, missing graph players, and underpowered magnitude tests). These pushed the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes: lock the definitions of L and reorganization, check player coverage first, set a minimum spell size, and pre-register the power and decision rule. The records did not block the study outright, since the absence setting produced a confirmed structural result in SF20.

blocking_constraints.text: 148 spells supports detection only of moderate correlations (about |rho| >= 0.23 at 80% power, two-sided). The stated MDE rho is not given numerically, and the record-level sample may be smaller after exclusions.
Reorganization relative to L has no validated operational definition or reliability estimate in the retrieved records; without it the predictor may be noise.
Player-level records are missing from the graph database in some cases (SF-APPS-009), so spells could be silently dropped or misattributed.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests offensive reorganization relative to L against change in PPP. The cited records are related but not the same question: SF20 addresses absence validation (structure shift confirmed, magnitude not), SF-APPS-009 and SF31 are data and small-n cautionary cases, and SF04 concerns trigger timing. They inform design risks but do not answer the question.

risks.text: 148 spells may be too few for small effects; subsets by absence type or season will be underpowered, as in SF20.
The reorganization index and L are undefined; reliability across games and seasons is unknown.
If L or the baseline uses any post-absence data, the estimate is biased toward a reorganization-outcome link.
Absences often follow poor stretches; change in PPP may reflect regression to the mean rather than reorganization.
Lineup quality, opponent strength, minutes, injury type and pace can move both reorganization and PPP.
Possessions per spell may be too few for stable per-spell PPP; small-possession cells inflate effects, as in SF31.
PPP change is derived from the same play-by-play used to define reorganization, risking shared-error coupling.
Missing player records in the graph (SF-APPS-009) could drop or misassign spells.
Several reorganization metrics, windows and playoff/regular-season splits invite selective reporting.
A placebo or null-absence baseline is needed; SF20 shows a structural shift can appear without a magnitude match, so placebo choice matters.
Four seasons with changing rules, pace and play-type coding may shift the baseline.

design.estimand: Within-spell association (Pearson or Spearman rho, plus a regression slope) between the offensive reorganization index in the post-absence window, measured relative to a pre-absence baseline L, and the change in PPP from pre- to post-absence windows.
design.unit: Player-absence spell (one row per spell), with team-game as a clustering unit.
design.sample: Pre-registered: spells with at least a fixed minimum of possessions in both windows (threshold set before analysis). Use 148 spells as the upper bound; report the count after exclusions. Exclude partial 2025-26 regular-season data before 2026-04-13 and any 2025-26 playoff data before 2026-06-21.
design.power: State the numeric MDE before the run. At n=148, two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power, the detectable |rho| is about 0.23; if the stated MDE is smaller, the study is underpowered and should be reported as such.
design.controls: Baseline L computed only from pre-absence games (no lookahead). Adjust for team and opponent strength, minutes, season, playoff status, pace, and lineup quality. Shrink per-spell PPP toward the season mean to reduce regression-to-the-mean. Cluster standard errors by team. Use a leave-one-season-out check.
design.falsification: Placebo spells drawn from matched non-absence stretches with the same design; the association should be null there. Pre-window trend test: reorganization should not predict PPP change before absence onset. A shifted-outcome check (lagging the outcome) should show no effect.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary metric and one primary window. Secondary metrics and subgroups (regular season vs playoffs, absence type) reported with Holm correction and labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported: primary rho's 95% CI excludes zero, is positive, and exceeds the placebo null distribution. Rejected: CI lies within +/-MDE of zero with adequate power. Otherwise uncertain. Artifact: if the effect vanishes after excluding spells with under the minimum possession threshold or after the lookahead-free baseline is used.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs (complete); 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21. Record the Neo4j coverage check and the list of missing players before any analysis.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: Does offensive reorganization relative to L predict change in points per possession?
What sample size and power are needed given n=148 spells and the stated minimum detectable effect rho?
How should reorganization be measured reliably and how should the baseline L be defined without leakage?
Are there regression-to-the-mean, selection, or confounding risks when conditioning on player absence?
args.query: Study of offensive reorganization during player absence and its association with change in points per possession, using NBA play-by-play, substitution intervals, and derived play-type possession records across 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons and playoffs.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
